# Helper: make swarm (beeswarm) points along x-axis
function swarm_along_x!(ax, x; y_pos=-1, swarm_width=0.5)
    xs = similar(x)
    for i in eachindex(x)
        xs[i] = x[i] + (rand() - 0.5) * swarm_width
    end
    scatter!(ax, xs, fill(y_pos, length(xs)), markersize=6, alpha=0.7)
    return ax
end

This could be the height of the **population** of **all** people in the world. The left example is a sub-population (or a sample).


<aside class="notes">
We are usually interested in the population of all humans. In order that statistical inference (according to Fisher) works, we do need to assume that the population is infite. The reason is, that else draws from the population that are not infinite are dependent on each other [source](https://www.repository.utl.pt/bitstream/10400.5/2327/1/wp022008.pdf). E.g. you have a population of five mice, two white and three black. If you sample three mice and all of them are black, you now know that the other mice are white. If the population would be infinite, you would not have that problem. This is more a minor detail, something to think about.

</aside>
